findings.reason: lec_start_xmit() saves lec_h = (struct lecdatahdr_8023 *)skb->data at net/atm/lec.c:244. On the short-frame path, when skb->len + skb_tailroom < LEC_MINIMUM_8023_SIZE, skb_copy_expand() at :263 builds a new skb and dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :266 frees the original head, so lec_h is dangling. The stale pointer is then unconditionally dereferenced: dst = lec_h->h_dest at :278 is fed into lec_arp_resolve() at :280, and lec_h->h_dest is printed at :286, :290, :302 (pr_debug only). The free is inside the same function (no helper trace needed), the skb is attacker-influenced data on the LANE netdev TX path (frame length attacker-chosen), and no re-derivation of lec_h from the new skb2 occurs. Counterevidence checked: the non-expanding path (enough tailroom) leaves lec_h valid, and the headroom-expansion path at :227-241 reassigns skb=skb2 before skb_push, so only the skb_copy_expand branch is affected.
findings.conclusion: lec_start_xmit() caches lec_h from skb->data at net/atm/lec.c:244, dev_kfree_skb at :266 after skb_copy_expand frees that head, and stale lec_h->h_dest is read at :278/:286/:290/:302 - a slab UAF read (high confidence, needs CONFIG_ATM LANE and a short frame).

findings.reason: send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into long-lived l2cap channel state: chan->data = skb at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:515 (comment 'Remember the skb so that we can send EAGAIN to the caller if we run out of credits'). bt_xmit() frees that skb via dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :622 (and send_mcast_pkt kfree_skb at :573) without clearing chan->data. The l2cap core then invokes the channel callbacks on remote-driven events: chan->ops->suspend(chan) at net/bluetooth/l2cap_core.c:1270 and :2484 (LE flow-control credit exhaustion) and chan->ops->resume(chan) at :5579 (credits received) and :7414 (encryption change, i.e. attacker-supplied HCI traffic). chan_suspend_cb()/chan_resume_cb() at 6lowpan.c:965-987 reload struct sk_buff *skb = chan->data (:967/:979) and WRITE lowpan_cb(skb)->status = -EAGAIN at :974 / = 0 at :986, i.e. a 4-byte write into skb->cb of the freed skb. IPSP channels are created with chan->mode = L2CAP_MODE_LE_FLOWCTL at 6lowpan.c:743, so the suspend/resume path is exactly the one that stores chan->data. Counterevidence checked: chan->data is never re-derived or cleared anywhere in 6lowpan.c; the only other readers are these two callbacks; the window is per-channel 'last skb sent', so the UAF write only lands when the remote peer triggers suspend/resume/encryption after the freed skb.
findings.conclusion: send_pkt() stores skb into chan->data (net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:515) that bt_xmit() then frees at :622, and remote-driven l2cap suspend/resume callbacks write lowpan_cb(skb)->status at :974/:986 through the dangling chan->data - a latent slab UAF write (medium confidence).

No stale hdr dereference after the free was found in this version.

coverage_gaps: A systematic sliding-window scan of all ~5000 kfree_skb/consume_skb/dev_kfree_skb sites in s02's net/ and drivers/net/ was not completed; only the fact-card variant shapes (atm/lec, bluetooth/6lowpan, iwlwifi tso, vcan) were verified in this session.

Pattern-2 sites storing skb->data-derived pointers into other long-lived state (driver/firmware private structs, timers, work items, per-socket state beyond net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c chan->data) were not enumerated in s02.
Frees that happen inside helper calls called between a pointer save and its use (dev_queue_xmit completion, netif_rx backlog drop, icmpv6_send, driver TX completion) were not traced in s02.

pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull/pskb_expand_head head-reallocation stale-pointer sites in s02 were deliberately excluded per branch instructions (other branches cover them; note fact i003 already covered s02 pull variants).
limitations: The lec.c finding requires CONFIG_ATM plus a LANE emulated LAN netdev and a frame shorter than LEC_MINIMUM_8023_SIZE with insufficient tailroom to take the skb_copy_expand path at :263; it is a local TX-path UAF read of a freed head (4-byte h_dest read into dst plus debug prints), not the seed's remote RX path.

The 6lowpan finding is a stored dangling pointer whose write (lowpan_cb(skb)->status, 4 bytes into freed skb->cb) requires the remote LE peer to trigger a suspend/resume or encryption event after the local side transmitted and freed a prior skb on the same IPSP channel; timing window per channel is bounded to the most recent skb.
No build, KASAN run, or reproducer was performed (read-only snapshot; all work confined to grep/reading of exact lines), so both findings are source-reading hypotheses.
Snapshot revision is opaque; line numbers and code state are valid only for snapshots/s02 as supplied, and no git history exists to check upstream fix status.
